addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

Here is my comprehensive report on all background workers, runners, and scheduling infrastructure in this codebase.

---

## Complete Report: Background Workers, Runners, and Scheduling Infrastructure

This is a Go-based server project ("Memos" -- an open source note-taking service). The server entry point is at `/bench/home/work/cmd/memos/main.go`, and the core server logic lives in `/bench/home/work/server/server.go`.

---

### 1. Server Entry Point and Startup Flow

**File:** `/bench/home/work/cmd/memos/main.go`
- Line 76: `server.NewServer(ctx, instanceProfile, storeInstance)` -- creates the server
- Line 89: `s.Start(ctx)` -- starts the HTTP server and background runners
- Lines 99-103: A goroutine is launched to listen for OS signals (SIGINT, SIGTERM) and trigger graceful shutdown via `s.Shutdown(ctx)`

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/server.go`
- The `Server` struct (line 31) stores `backgroundRunnerCancels []context.CancelFunc` and `backgroundRunnerWG sync.WaitGroup` for managing background runner lifecycle.
- Line 129 in `Start()`: calls `s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)` after the HTTP server goroutine is launched.
- Lines 124-128: The HTTP server itself runs in a goroutine (`go func() { s.httpServer.Serve(listener) }`)

---

### 2. Background Workers/Runners ACTIVELY Started by the Server

#### 2A. S3 Presign Runner (ACTIVE -- started by server)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`

This is the only background runner explicitly started by the server's `startBackgroundRunners()` method.

- **Type:** `Runner` struct (line 16) with a `Store` field
- **Constructor:** `NewRunner(store)` at line 20
- **Interval-based scheduling:** Runs every 12 hours (`const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, line 27)
- **`Run(ctx)` method (line 29):** Uses `time.NewTicker(runnerInterval)` to periodically call `RunOnce(ctx)`. Runs in a loop until context is canceled.
- **`RunOnce(ctx)` method (line 43):** Calls `CheckAndPresign(ctx)` which iterates over all S3-backed attachments in batches of 100, regenerating presigned URLs for any whose presigned URL will expire within 4 days (presigned URLs have a 5-day expiration).

**How it is started** (in `/bench/home/work/server/server.go`, lines 153-174):
```go
s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)
s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)    // immediate first run (synchronous)

s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)
go func() {                      // continuous run in a goroutine
    defer s.backgroundRunnerWG.Done()
    s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)
}()
```

**Shutdown:** The runner's context is canceled via `s.stopBackgroundRunners()` (line 176), and the server waits for the WaitGroup in `waitBackgroundRunners()` (line 184).

#### 2B. Cache Cleanup Goroutines (ACTIVE -- started implicitly via store)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/store/cache/cache.go`

The cache system runs background cleanup goroutines. Each `Cache` instance starts a goroutine upon construction.

- **Constructor:** `New(config)` at line 76 launches `go c.cleanupLoop()` (line 83)
- **`cleanupLoop()` (line 200):** Uses `time.NewTicker(c.config.CleanupInterval)` to periodically call `cleanup()`, which removes expired cache items. Default cleanup interval is 5 minutes (line 48).
- **Shutdown:** `Close()` (line 186) sends on `stopChan` and waits for the `closedChan` to confirm the goroutine exited.

**How they are started:** Three cache instances are created in `/bench/home/work/store/store.go` lines 51-53:
```go
instanceSettingCache: cache.New(cacheConfig),
userCache:            cache.New(cacheConfig),
userSettingCache:     cache.New(cacheConfig),
```
Each one launches its own cleanup goroutine. They are closed in `Store.Close()` (lines 73-76).

#### 2C. Webhook Async Dispatch Workers (ACTIVE -- started via package init)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go`

- Lines 39-55: In the `init()` function, a buffered channel `asyncPostQueue` (capacity 128) is created, and **4 goroutines** are spawned to consume from it. Each goroutine runs `webhook.Post(payload)` for each payload received from the queue.
- These goroutines are started at package initialization time (when the webhook package is first imported) and run for the lifetime of the process.
- There is no explicit shutdown mechanism for these workers -- they rely on process exit.

**Callers:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`
- Line 43: `webhook.PostAsync(payload)` (for memo comment created webhooks)
- Line 71: `webhook.PostAsync(payload)` (for memo created/updated/deleted webhooks)

#### 2D. Email Async Dispatch Workers (ACTIVE -- started via package init)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/email/email.go`

- Lines 14-36: In the `init()` function, a buffered channel `asyncEmailQueue` (capacity 128) is created, and **2 goroutines** are spawned to consume from it. Each goroutine runs `email.Send(request.config, request.message)` for each request received from the queue.
- These goroutines are started at package initialization time and run for the lifetime of the process.
- There is no explicit shutdown mechanism.

**Callers:** `/bench/home/work/server/notification/email.go` line 30 sets `email.SendAsync` as the default sender for `EmailDispatcher`. It is invoked through the notification dispatch chain:
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/notification_email.go` line 21-22: creates `EmailDispatcher` and calls `DispatchInboxEmail`, which ultimately calls `email.SendAsync`.
- This is triggered by memo comment creation (`memo_service_comments.go` line 101) and memo mention creation (`memo_mention_helpers.go` line 124).

#### 2E. SSE Hub and Heartbeat (ACTIVE -- per-connection)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`
- `SSEHub` (line 56) manages client subscriptions. Created at line 57 of `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` via `NewSSEHub()`.
- The hub is stored on the `Server` struct at `/bench/home/work/server/server.go` line 38 and closed during shutdown at line 206.

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`
- Line 64: Each SSE connection creates a `time.NewTicker(sseHeartbeatInterval)` (30 seconds, line 16) for sending heartbeat pings to keep connections alive.
- The SSE handler runs a blocking loop (lines 80-109) per connected client, listening on client events, heartbeat ticks, and context cancellation.

#### 2F. PAT Last-Used Timestamp Update (ACTIVE -- fire-and-forget goroutine)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go`
- Lines 179-185: `recordPATUsage()` launches a `go func()` to asynchronously update a Personal Access Token's last-used timestamp in the database. This is a fire-and-forget goroutine spawned on each authenticated PAT request.

---

### 3. Scheduling Infrastructure That EXISTS But Is NOT Used by the Server

#### 3A. Cron Scheduler Package (UNUSED by server)

**Directory:** `/bench/home/work/internal/scheduler/`

This is a fully-featured cron job scheduler that is **never imported or used** by any non-test production code.

Files:
- `/bench/home/work/internal/scheduler/doc.go` -- Package documentation
- `/bench/home/work/internal/scheduler/scheduler.go` -- Core `Scheduler` type with `New()`, `Register()`, `Start()`, `Stop()` methods
- `/bench/home/work/internal/scheduler/job.go` -- `Job` struct with Name, Schedule (cron expression), Handler, Timezone, Tags fields
- `/bench/home/work/internal/scheduler/parser.go` -- Full cron expression parser supporting 5-field and 6-field formats, with wildcards, ranges, lists, and steps
- `/bench/home/work/internal/scheduler/middleware.go` -- Middleware system including `Recovery()`, `Logging()`, `Timeout()`, and `Chain()`

Key features of this unused scheduler:
- Supports standard cron expressions (minute hour day month weekday) and 6-field format with seconds
- Timezone-aware scheduling (per-job and global timezone)
- Middleware pattern (logging, recovery from panics, timeouts)
- Graceful shutdown with context cancellation
- Each job runs in its own goroutine with a timer-based loop

The scheduler is only imported in its own test files:
- `/bench/home/work/internal/scheduler/example_test.go`
- `/bench/home/work/internal/scheduler/integration_test.go`

#### 3B. Memo Payload Runner (PARTIALLY UNUSED -- exists but NOT started as a background runner)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`

- **Type:** `Runner` struct (line 14) with `Store` and `MarkdownService` fields
- **Constructor:** `NewRunner(store, markdownService)` at line 19
- **`RunOnce(ctx)` method (line 27):** Iterates over ALL memos in batches of 100, calling `RebuildMemoPayload()` on each to re-extract tags and properties from the memo content.
- **No `Run()` method** -- unlike the S3 presign runner, this runner has no interval-based continuous execution loop.

**How it IS used:** The `RebuildMemoPayload()` function (line 74) is imported and called directly (not via the Runner) in:
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 108 (when creating a memo)
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 447 (when updating a memo)

**How it is NOT used:** The `Runner` struct and its `RunOnce()` method (which processes all memos in bulk) are never instantiated or called from the server startup code. The runner infrastructure exists but is not wired into `startBackgroundRunners()`.

---

### 4. Summary Table

| Component | Location | Type | Active? | How Started |
|-----------|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| S3 Presign Runner | `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go` | Interval (12h ticker) | YES | `server.go:startBackgroundRunners()` as goroutine |
| Cache Cleanup (x3) | `store/cache/cache.go` | Interval (5min ticker) | YES | Implicitly via `cache.New()` in `store/store.go` |
| Webhook Workers (x4) | `internal/webhook/webhook.go` | Queue consumer (chan) | YES | Package `init()` |
| Email Workers (x2) | `internal/email/email.go` | Queue consumer (chan) | YES | Package `init()` |
| SSE Hub + Heartbeat | `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`, `sse_handler.go` | Per-connection ticker (30s) | YES | Per SSE connection |
| PAT Usage Recorder | `server/auth/authenticator.go:180` | Fire-and-forget goroutine | YES | Per PAT auth request |
| HTTP Server | `server/server.go:124` | Goroutine | YES | `server.Start()` |
| Signal Handler | `cmd/memos/main.go:99` | Goroutine | YES | Main function |
| Cron Scheduler | `internal/scheduler/` (all files) | Cron-based scheduler | **NO** | Never imported in production code |
| Memo Payload Runner | `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` | Batch runner (no loop) | **PARTIAL** | Only `RebuildMemoPayload()` function used; the `Runner.RunOnce()` bulk method is never called |

- **Email Dispatch Workers (×2 goroutines)** — channel-consumer queue (`asyncEmailQueue`, capacity 128); send notification emails (`internal/email/email.go:14–36`; started in package `init()`)
- **SSE Heartbeat** — 30-second `time.Ticker` per connected SSE client; sends keep-alive pings (`server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go:64`)

**Unused scheduling infrastructure:**

- **`internal/scheduler/` package** — A fully-featured cron-expression-based job scheduler with middleware support (recovery, logging, timeout), timezone-aware scheduling, and graceful shutdown. - **Memo Payload Runner** (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`) — Has a `Runner` struct with a bulk `RunOnce()` method that rebuilds all memo payloads in batches, but the runner is **never instantiated or started** by `startBackgroundRunners()`.
